selection_reason: No experiments have been completed, so the key uncertainty is whether a simple RNA-only model is already strong and whether multimodal fusion is needed at all. config_026 tests a minimal, strong RNA baseline using scGPT with a single profile and no aggregation or fusion. This will establish a reference for RNA performance and enable a direct follow-up comparison with config_001, which keeps the same RNA encoder and profile setting while adding a ResNet50 image branch and concat fusion, thereby isolating the contribution of image information. This is a budget-efficient first step because it avoids assuming multimodal complexity is necessary and sets up a clean comparison of an important design choice.

The only completed run is a single-profile RNA-only scGPT baseline with validation accuracy 0.4106, so there is still no evidence about whether image data is informative. config_040 tests a minimal image-only single-profile ResNet50 baseline, isolating the image representation/modality without adding aggregation or fusion. This is the best next use of budget because it reduces uncertainty about a central design choice, provides a necessary unimodal baseline for later multimodal comparisons, and avoids assuming that a multimodal model will outperform simpler models.

The RNA-only scGPT singleprofile result is much stronger than image-only ResNet50, but the image result is sparse and may reflect a weak encoder rather than the image modality itself. config_041 tests a stronger image encoder, ViT-L, while keeping image-only and singleprofile fixed, isolating the image representation choice. This is the best next step because it provides a clean comparison to config_040 and reduces uncertainty about whether image features are worth adding before testing multimodal fusion or more complex profile/aggregation settings.

Existing evidence shows single-profile scGPT RNA is much stronger than either image-only encoder (accuracy 0.411 vs 0.227/0.208; F1 0.378 vs 0.191/0.172), but it is unclear whether image features can add complementary signal when fused with RNA. config_047 keeps the strongest RNA encoder and single-profile setting, adds the better image-only encoder (ViT-L), and uses simple concat fusion, so it directly tests whether multimodal fusion improves over the RNA-only baseline without introducing multiprofile aggregation or weighted fusion. This is the best next step because it isolates the key modality/fusion question and will determine whether further multimodal complexity is worth the limited budget.

RNA-only scGPT is the strongest single-modality baseline, image-only models are weak with ViT-L only slightly better than ResNet50, and the current best multimodal model uses scGPT + ViT-L with concat fusion. It is unclear whether the multimodal gain depends specifically on ViT-L or would persist with a weaker image encoder. config_001 keeps scGPT, singleprofile, and concat fusion fixed while changing only the image encoder to ResNet50, isolating the image representation effect. This is a minimal, informative comparison that helps decide whether to keep investing in ViT-L or whether simpler image encoders are sufficient before testing more complex fusion or multiprofile settings.

The strongest completed result is config_047, a single-profile multimodal model using scGPT, ImageNet ViT-L, and concat fusion, with the best accuracy and F1. The main untested factor in this best setting is fusion: concat has been tested, but weighted fusion has not. config_004 changes only the fusion method while keeping the modality, profile setting, RNA encoder, and image encoder fixed, so it directly tests whether learned weighting improves over simple concatenation. This is the best next experiment because it is a low-confounding extension of the current best direction, helps isolate the effect of fusion, and avoids introducing multiprofile aggregation or a new RNA encoder before the simpler single-profile design is better understood.

The strongest completed result is config_047, using scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + concat in a singleprofile multimodal setting, while image-only models are weak and weighted fusion is slightly worse. The main unresolved question is whether multiprofile aggregation can improve on this best singleprofile core. config_017 keeps the best RNA encoder, image encoder, and fusion while changing to multiprofile with the simplest aggregation, avgpool, so it tests the profile/aggregation axis without changing representation or fusion. Under limited budget, this is the best next experiment because it exploits the most promising direction while reducing uncertainty about one of the largest untested design choices.

The strongest evidence so far is config_017, where multiprofile scgpt + ViT-L with avgpool and concat reaches 0.518 accuracy and 0.484 F1, far above single-profile multimodal baselines. However, only one multiprofile aggregation strategy has been tested, so it is unclear whether avgpool is sufficient or whether transformer aggregation can further improve profile integration. config_020 changes only aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping the same model setting, profile setting, RNA encoder, image encoder, and concat fusion. This isolates the effect of aggregation, exploits the currently best direction, and is a high-value next experiment under a limited budget.

The strongest result is multiprofile multimodal scgpt+ViT with avgpool/concat (0.5176 acc, 0.4837 F1), but the source of the large multiprofile gain is unclear: it may come from aggregating RNA profiles alone, image profiles alone, or multimodal synergy. config_022 keeps the strong scgpt RNA encoder and uses avgpool, the aggregation favored by config_017 over transformer, while removing image and fusion. It directly tests whether multiprofile RNA alone improves over the 0.4106 RNA-only singleprofile baseline. This is a high-value, simpler-model experiment because it isolates the profile-setting/aggregation effect and will tell whether future budget should focus on RNA profile aggregation or multimodal fusion, rather than exploiting the current best without understanding why it works.

Multiprofile + avgpool is the strongest evidence so far, with rna_only scgpt avgpool best (acc 0.5305, F1 0.5152) and multimodal scgpt/vit_l avgpool concat close but lower. The main untested uncertainty is whether this result depends specifically on scgpt or on multiprofile RNA representation generally. config_015 keeps the promising multiprofile/avgpool/RNA-only setting and changes only the RNA encoder to scvi_n200, isolating the representation effect. This is a better use of budget than another multimodal tweak because multimodal has not yet beaten the simpler RNA-only model, and clarifying RNA encoder importance may guide both high-accuracy selection and model simplification.
